newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hochtief on Holzmann supervisory board.
newsitem.headline: Hochtief on Holzmann supervisory board.

text.p: Germany's largest building group, Philip Holzmann AG, said on Friday it planned to offer a place on its supervisory board to a representative of Hochtief AG, Germany's second largest construction firm.
Holzmann said the Hochtief representative, which has yet to be named by Hochtief, would be appointed to the board "in the medium-term".

A spokesman for Holzmann said Hochtief had asked for representation on the supervisory board, which has an advisory role similar to that of the U.S. board of directors, to reflect the fact that it is a major shareholder in Holzmann.
Hochtief has for some time had a stake of 20 percent in Holzmann, with the possibility of acquiring a further 14.9 percent in two tranches of 4.9 percent and 10 percent.

A spokesman for Holzmann said the appointment had no "immediate connection" to the two companies' continued talks on how they can more closely cooperate, talks that the spokesman said had so far not produced an agreement.
Holzmann said the appointment had been supported both by the Holzmann board and of Deutsche Bank AG, the other main shareholder with 25.8 percent.
The Federal Cartel Office is due to begin hearings into the two group's plans for increased cooperation on April 9, including Hochtief's wish to increase its stake.
